extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of English poetry; literature students and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and critical principles for judging major English poets (Chaucer, Spenser, Shakespeare, Milton), focusing on language, versification, characterization, dramatic vs. epic effects, and imaginative power. Derived from a lecture-format critical essay comparing their strengths and modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathos of sentiment and romance (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: He has not indeed the pathos of immediate action or suffering, which is more properly the dramatic; but he has all the pathos of sentiment and romance — all that belongs to distant objects of terror, and uncertain, imaginary distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: the Cave of Despair, the Cave of Mammon, and the account of Malbecco's change into Jealousy; Spenser's pathos is suited to remote, visionary objects rather than immediate dramatic action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength as vastness and sublimity (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: His strength ... is not strength of will or action, of bone and muscle, nor is it coarse and palpable — but it assumes a character of vastness and sublimity seen through the same visionary medium, and blended with the appalling associations of preternatural agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess strength by grandeur and preternatural, sublime effect (e.g., 'The Cave of Mammon' stanzas), not by muscular or dramatic force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Richness and copiousness of language (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: The language of Spenser is full, and copious, to overflowing: it is less pure and idiomatic than Chaucer's, and is enriched and adorned with phrases borrowed from the different languages of Europe, both ancient and modern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both the lavishness and the impurity/trade-offs: richness and ornament vs. idiomatic purity; context: sometimes license is a consequence of stanzaic demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versification: smooth, sounding, musical undulations (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: His versification is, at once, the most smooth and the most sounding in the language. It is a labyrinth of sweet sounds, 'in many a winding bout of linked sweetness long drawn out'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the poet's control of sound, melody, pauses, and modulation; the effect may lull or enchant, and requires variety to avoid cloying sweetness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stanza-form suitability and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: This stanza, with alternate and repeatedly recurring rhymes, is borrowed from the Italians. It was peculiarly fitted to their language, which abounds in similar vowel terminations, and is as little adapted to ours...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge technical form by fit to language: stanzaic forms imported from other tongues may force 'license of expression' or produce new poetic language; consider whether form aids or hampers expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial/picturesque imagination (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions (e.g., Procession of the Passions, Mask of Cupid, Satyrane taming lion's whelps) have a high picturesque character, reminding one of Rubens's allegorical pictures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value richly visual, painterly description and allegorical tableau; compare poetical fancy to pictorial composition and colour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and beauty in allegory/mask-scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the same kind with the Procession of the Passions, as little obscure, and still more beautiful, is the Mask of Cupid, with his train of votaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess allegorical passages for intelligibility and aesthetic beauty (not necessarily obscurity); successful mask-scenes combine clear allegorical figures with attractive description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness, novelty, and love of the marvellous (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: As poets, imagination was common to them all: but the principle or moving power ... in Spenser, novelty, and the love of the marvellous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure originality and appetite for wonder/novelty; novelty may be a defining virtue insofar as it energizes imaginative landscapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poet of manners / realism (Chaucer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chaucer excels as the poet of manners, or of real life; Chaucer most frequently describes things as they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Chaucer by verisimilitude, faithful depiction of everyday life and social types, and observational accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remoteness and romance as a mode (Spenser)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spenser, as the poet of romance; Chaucer most frequently describes things as they are; Spenser, as we wish them to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the poet's mode is remote/romantic (idealized, visionary) versus realistic; remoteness can be a deliberate aesthetic choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic quality and universality (Shakespeare)
rubrics_metrics.description: The striking peculiarity of Shakspeare's mind was its generic quality, its power of communication with all other minds — so that it contained a universe of thought and feeling within itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Shakespeare (or any poet) by scope and capacity to encompass varied human types and experiences; universality of insight is a key merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth and individuality of conception (Shakespeare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of his characters is as much itself, and as absolutely independent of the rest, as well as of the author, as if they were living persons, not fictions of the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how fully characters appear as independent, self-consistent persons; examples: Caliban, Prospero, Hamlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic characterization through action and contrast (Shakespeare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspeare's are historical figures, equally true and correct, but put into action, where every nerve and muscle is displayed in the struggle with others, with all the effect of collision and contrast, with every variety of light and shade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value characters that change and reveal subordinate traits in new situations; dramatic interplay and conflict should produce character development, not static portraiture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and spontaneity of dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: The dialogues in Shakspeare are carried on without any consciousness of what is to follow, without any appearance of preparation or premeditation ... like our dreams we hold conversations with ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dialogue for immediacy, unpredictability, and the sense that speech issues from character rather than authorial contrivance; natural-sounding exchanges are prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and evocative power of epithet/phrase
rubrics_metrics.description: A word, an epithet paints a whole scene, or throws us back whole years in the history of the person represented. (Example: Prospero's 'Me and thy crying self' brings infancy to mind.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for economical phrasing that summons broad context or history; a single well-chosen epithet can evoke a scene or backstory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic fluctuation and complexity of passion (Shakespeare)
rubrics_metrics.description: The passion in Shakspeare ... is not some one habitual feeling ... it is passion modified by passion ... irritated by obstacles or yielding to them; rising from small beginnings to its utmost height ... now drunk with hope, now stung to madness, now sunk in despair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the emotional dynamism: passions should be multi-layered, interacting, and capable of sudden changes; dramatic poetry rewards volatility and complexity of feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic/imaginative passion: distance, magnitude, contemplation (Milton)
rubrics_metrics.description: Milton takes the imaginative part of passion — that which remains after the event, which the mind reposes on when all is over, which looks upon circumstances from the remotest elevation of thought and fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For epic or contemplative poetry, assess how passion is transmuted into imaginative grandeur and universality rather than immediate dramatic impulse; epic effects inspire admiration by magnitude and permanence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of the preternatural with natural truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Airy beings waited at his call, and came at his bidding ... The world of spirits lay open to him, like the world of real men and women: and there is the same truth in his delineations of the one as of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge supernatural characters by the same standards as human ones: they should speak, feel, and act with believable inner logic and individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency vs. variety in character portraiture (Chaucer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chaucer's characters are consistent, but uniform; we get no new idea of them from first to last; they are like portraits or physiognomical studies ... that preserve the same unaltered air and attitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistency as a strength for clear types, but penalize lack of internal variety or development when dramatic variety is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sensory detail and intuitive natural observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of intuitive power bringing every object in nature, whether present or absent, before the mind's eye (examples: Ophelia's willow image; Cleopatra's 'my serpent of old Nile').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess author's capacity to invoke sensory particulars that make scenes believable and immediate; details should feel observed, not invented for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding 'cloying' sweetness through modulation and variety
rubrics_metrics.description: His versification ... would cloy by their very sweetness, but that the ear is constantly relieved and enchanted by their continued variety of modulation — dwelling on the pauses of the action, or flowing on in a fuller tide of harmony with the movement of the sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate musicality not only for prettiness but for controlled variety; sustained sweetness must be counterbalanced by modulation, pauses, and shifts to maintain effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of dramatic directions and concrete stage cues
rubrics_metrics.description: Shakspeare always gives the best directions for the costume and carriage of his heroes. Thus ... Ophelia gives the following account of Hamlet ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess texts for embedded practical cues (costume, carriage, gesture) that render characters performable and vivid on stage as well as on the page.
